title: Drop One Digit for the Biggest Number
statement:
You get a positive integer as a string number and a character digit. The digit occurs in the number at least once.

Remove exactly one occurrence of digit from number. Choose which occurrence so that the remaining number is as large as possible, and return it as a string.

examples.why: Removing the first 4 lets the 7 behind it move up to the front. Removing the last 4 gives only 477.
The first 3 is followed by a bigger digit, so removing it lets the 9 move up: 993. Removing the last 3 gives only 939.
No 5 is followed by a bigger digit. Removing the first 5 lets the 4 into the front place (455); removing the last 5 only changes the final place (545).

constraints: digit is a digit 1–9 that occurs in number
hints: All candidates have the same length, so the biggest one is the one with the larger digit at the first place where they differ.
Removing the digit at position i shifts number[i + 1] into place i. That is a gain exactly when number[i + 1] is bigger than the digit.
Remove the first occurrence followed by a bigger digit. If there is none, remove the last occurrence, so the damage happens as far right as possible.

explain.intuition:
Every candidate result has the same length, so comparing them is like comparing strings: the first differing place decides. Removing occurrence i leaves everything before i unchanged and slides number[i + 1] into position i.

If that next digit is larger than digit, the number improves at position i, and the earlier the improvement, the more it is worth. So take the first such occurrence. If no occurrence is followed by a larger digit, every removal makes things worse or equal at its position, and the best you can do is push that loss as far right as possible: remove the last occurrence.
steps: Scan i from left to right. Remember the last index where number[i] === digit.
If number[i] === digit and i + 1 < n and number[i + 1] > digit, return the string without position i.
After the scan, return the string without the last remembered position.
pitfalls: Always removing the first occurrence. In "5455" that gives 455, while removing the last 5 gives 545.
Always removing the last occurrence. In "4747" that gives 477 instead of 747.
Converting to a number to compare candidates; 100 digits overflow every built-in integer type. Compare strings of equal length instead.

solutions.title: Try every occurrence
solutions.idea: Build the string without each occurrence and keep the largest. Equal-length digit strings compare correctly as text.

solutions.title: Greedy: first occurrence before a bigger digit
solutions.idea: Remove the first occurrence whose next digit is bigger; if none exists, remove the last occurrence.

followups: Remove exactly k digits of any kind to make the number as large as possible. What structure does the greedy need now?
Make the result as small as possible instead. Which comparison flips?
lcTitle: Remove Digit From Number to Maximize Result
